summary.text: A 65-year-old African-American woman with lymphoma in remission and several other past medical conditions presented with a black facial lesion that had been progressively enlarging and irritating her skin. She smoked one pack of cigarettes per day. Examination showed a 2 x 1-cm black plaque in the right preauricular area.

A superficial shave biopsy of the upper portion of the lesion showed acanthosis with heavily pigmented basaloid cells, melanophages and dermal inflammation, with dendritic melanocytes on MART-1 staining; the Figure 2 caption adds hyperkeratosis, hyperpigmentation throughout the epidermis and lymphocytic perivascular inflammation. Clinicopathologic correlation established irritated melanoacanthoma, and she denied further intervention.

She returned several months later with the lesion persisting and larger. A deep shave biopsy to confirm the diagnosis and exclude malignant melanoma showed the same pathology as the first biopsy, the melanoacanthoma diagnosis was reaffirmed, and the biopsy site healed without recurrence.

summary.text: An 85-year-old Haitian-Creole man with a history of hepatitis B and hepatitis C, and no personal or family history of melanoma or other skin cancers, presented with an asymptomatic mass that had been present for over a year and progressively enlarging. A comprehensive systemic review revealed no pertinent abnormalities.

Examination revealed a large 3 x 2.5-cm lobulated, exophytic, black nodule with surrounding hyperpigmentation, favored clinically to be nodular malignant melanoma, with no palpable lymphadenopathy. Black plaques on the left posterior shoulder and left axilla were thought to be pigmented seborrheic keratoses. Excisional shave biopsies were performed.

Microscopy of the nodule showed papillomatosis, acanthosis, hyperkeratosis and heavily pigmented melanocytes and melanophages, establishing melanoacanthoma. The shoulder and axilla lesions showed acanthosis with dermal melanin deposits and basal hyperpigmentation, establishing pigmented seborrheic keratosis. All biopsy sites healed without complication and follow-up examination did not reveal recurrence.

Microscopic presentation of pigmented seborrheic keratoses on the left posterior shoulder and left axilla of an 85-year-old man with concurrent melanoacanthoma on his left lower abdomen.
